title: Historic 36% Reduction in Daily Incidence of Femicides in Mexico, Reports the Secretariat of Women
author: Emir Olivares and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by[Emir Olivares and Alonso
Urrutia](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Emir%20Olivares%20y%20Alonso%20Urrutia)
originally appeared in the [October 5, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/05/politica/reduccion-
historica-de-36-en-incidencia-diaria-de-feminicidios-refiere-la-secretaria-de-
las-mujeres), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. In more than a year of operation, the Women's Line (079
option 1) has identified femicidal violence in **33 percent** of the 20,000
calls that this tool has received, reported the head of the Secretariat of
Women, Laura Itzel Castillo.

Participating in this Monday's presidential mañanera, the official noted that
having detected those risks "made it possible to prevent the manifestation of
this form of violence."

According to data from that agency, under this administration "there has been
a historic drop" of **36 percent in the incidence of the daily average of
femicides** , pointed out Ingrid Gómez, Undersecretary for the Right to a Life
Free of Violence, Secretariat of Women.

The line aims to protect the rights of all women in the country. To date,
Secretary Castillo stated, 83 percent of the calls registered at this number
correspond to care for some type of violence and 17 percent to guidance and
information.

> If you are experiencing violence and don't know what to do, call 079 option
> 1.
>
> Secretary of Women Laura Itzel Castillo

Meanwhile, the federal president outlined that when a woman experiences
violence and calls 079 option 1, "it is not only the call per se and the
person who is answering it, but it is channeled. So, the Security secretariats
or the women's institutes or secretariats of the states are asked to approach
the woman to attend to her."

She added that even if after some time the possible victim does not call, the
woman is called back to find out how she is and whether she needs any type of
support.

Secretary Castillo added that the federal government has established **1,001
LIBRE centers** in all the states of the Republic, where 1,436,869 services
have been provided to date and 656,344 people have been attended.

The total number of LIBRE centers created so far, she maintained, covers 40
percent of the country's municipalities.

In these spaces "women strengthen their community networks and develop their
leadership, they are free and nearby, where psycho-emotional support and legal
advice are provided, rights training and self-training for economic autonomy
are carried out, and work is done on the prevention of violence with training
workshops."

Likewise, there are so far **197,446 volunteer women** registered in the
Tejedoras de la Patria Network.
